resources.string: Two identical chows in the same suit.
Two chows of the same numbers in two different suits.
Two chows of one suit that follow each other, making a six-tile straight.
1-2-3 and 7-8-9 chows of the same suit.
A pung or kong of 1s, 9s or winds. A dragon pung scores 2 points.
A kong claimed from a discard or made by adding a tile to a melded pung.
A hand with tiles of only two of the three suits.
A hand of suit tiles only, without winds or dragons.
Waiting only for a 3 to make 1-2-3, or only for a 7 to make 7-8-9. Not valid if waiting on more than one tile.
Waiting only for the middle tile of a chow. Not valid if waiting on more than one tile.

Going out on a tile drawn from the wall.
Each flower or season scores 1 point. Flowers do not count for the 8 points needed to win.
A pung or kong of dragons.
A pung or kong of the wind of the current round.
A pung or kong of the player's seat wind. The dealer is East, then South, West and North counter-clockwise.
A concealed hand, without melded sets, going out on a discard.
Four chows and a pair, without honors.
All four tiles of a kind used in the hand, without declaring a kong.
Two pungs or kongs of the same number in two different suits.

A hand without terminals (1 and 9) or honors.
Every set, including the pair, has a terminal (1 or 9) or an honor.
A hand completed without melds, going out on a tile drawn from the wall.
Two melded kongs. A melded and a concealed kong score 6 points.
Going out on the last tile of its kind: the other three are visible in the discards or the melds.
Four pungs or kongs and a pair.
Tiles of only one of the three suits together with honors.
Three chows, one in each suit, each shifted up one number from the last.

Two pungs or kongs of dragons.
A 1 to 9 straight made of chows of the three suits.

Three chows of the same numbers, one in each suit.
Three pungs or kongs, one in each suit, each shifted one up from the last.
A hand that would otherwise score no points, without counting the flowers.
Going out on the very last tile of the wall.
Going out on the last tile of the game, discarded by another player.
Going out on the replacement tile drawn after a kong (not after a flower).
Going out on the tile another player adds to a melded pung to make a kong.
Single honors and single tiles of separate knitted sequences (1-4-7, 2-5-8 and 3-6-9, each of a different suit), without a pair.
A straight made of three knitted sequences, such as 1-4-7 of dots, 2-5-8 of characters and 3-6-9 of bamboos.
A hand made up only of 6, 7, 8 and 9 tiles.
A hand made up only of 1, 2, 3 and 4 tiles.

1 to 9 of one suit, forming three consecutive chows.

Every set and the pair include a 5.
Three pungs or kongs of the same number, one in each suit.
Three concealed pungs or kongs, made without melding.
A hand formed by seven pairs.
The seven honors and seven tiles of separate knitted sequences, such as 1-4-7 of bamboos, 2-5-8 of characters and 3-6-9 of dots, without a pair.
Pungs or kongs and a pair of 2, 4, 6 and 8 tiles only.
A hand formed entirely of one suit.
Three chows of the same numbers in the same suit.
Three pungs or kongs of the same suit, each shifted one up from the last.
A hand made up only of 7, 8 and 9 tiles.
A hand made up only of 4, 5 and 6 tiles.
A hand made up only of 1, 2 and 3 tiles.
Four chows of one suit, each shifted up one or two numbers from the last, but not a mix of both.

Four chows of the same numbers in the same suit.

Pungs or kongs of all four winds.
